title: Exact dimer ground states of long-range spin chains and ladders
abstract: Interacting spin chains and ladders are known to support a plethora of quantum phases with complex ground-state phase diagrams. In this work, we study a large family of such models and determine precise, explicit conditions under which an exact dimer state is guaranteed to be the ground state. These general conditions are validated for various generalizations of the Majumdar-Ghosh model using exact diagonalization. Our results provide exact reference points in the phase diagrams of a wide class of spin chains and ladders, including those with anisotropic and arbitrary-range interactions.
summary: This paper rigorously determines the conditions under which exotic dimer states are guaranteed to be the ground state in generalized spin chains and ladders with long-range and anisotropic interactions. By combining theoretical semi-positivity arguments with numerical validation, it maps out precise phase boundaries that extend the known understanding of quantum magnetism.
main_problem: The core problem is determining precise, explicit conditions on coupling constants for long-range interacting spin chains and ladders to guarantee that the exact dimer state is the ground state.
main_result: The authors derive sufficient conditions (e.g., involving non-negativity of auxiliary coefficients $\alpha_n$ and $ eta_n$) under which the dimer state is guaranteed to be the ground state, often extending beyond previously known necessary conditions.
method: The methodology combines theoretical derivation using semi-positivity arguments on the Hamiltonian ($ ar{H} \ge 0$) with validation via exact diagonalization (ED) for finite systems and analysis of anisotropic quantum top models.
model_or_system: The study focuses on spin-1/2 interacting quantum spin chains and ladders, described by generalized Hamiltonians including long-range interactions ($J_n$ and $K_n$) and anisotropy terms ($\gamma_\mu^n$).
key_observables: Ground state energy (EGS), Dimer entanglement entropy ($\Delta S_{	ext{dimer}}$), and the non-negativity of derived coefficients ($\alpha_n,  eta_n$).
important_parameters: Coupling constants $\{J_n\}, \{K_n\}$, anisotropy parameters $\{\gamma_\mu^n\}$, and system size $L$ (often assumed even).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a ground state characterized by semi-positivity, and some derivations rely on finite-size approximations or specific structural assumptions about coupling ranges.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing boundaries between Dimer, Ferromagnetic (FM), and Partially Magnetized states for both isotropic and anisotropic chains/ladders, comparing theoretical predictions with ED results.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general Hamiltonian forms to deriving necessary conditions via semi-positivity arguments ($\alpha_n \ge 0,  eta_n \ge 0$). It then tackles the complexity of anisotropy by relating it to quantum top spectra and concludes by comparing theoretical sufficient conditions against numerical ED results on phase diagrams.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical criteria for identifying specific quantum phases (dimerized) in complex, interacting many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding magnetic materials where long-range correlations are important.
